subject: Agriculture
title: Right to Food
description: A 60-second lesson on Right to Food.

hook.text: The UN declared food a human right in 1948. Seventy-five years later, 735 million people still can't exercise it.

buildup.text: Over 30 countries have enshrined the right to food in their constitutions. Enforcement is the gap.

discovery.text: Brazil's Zero Hunger program lifted 30 million people out of food insecurity through school meals and cash transfers.

twist.text: When political leadership changed, Brazil's food security gains were partially reversed. Rights need sustained commitment.

climax.text: Making food a legally enforceable right—not just a goal—gives courts power to hold governments accountable.

punchline.text: A right without enforcement is a suggestion. Hungry people need more than words.

quiz.question: How many people did Brazil's Zero Hunger lift out of food insecurity?

details.summary: The right to food is a human right recognized in international law that obligates governments to ensure their citizens can feed themselves in dignity. This topic covers legal frameworks, enforcement challenges, and how countries implement this right in practice.
details.whyItMatters: Despite being enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the right to food remains unfulfilled for over 700 million hungry people. Making it legally enforceable is key to ending hunger.
takeaways: The right to food is recognized in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Article 25)
Over 30 countries have enshrined the right to food in their national constitutions
Legal enforceability varies widely—India's landmark law guarantees subsidized grain

faq.question: What does the right to food mean in international law?
faq.answer: The right to food obliges governments to respect, protect, and fulfill access to adequate food. States must not obstruct food access, must prevent others from doing so, and must proactively help those unable to feed themselves.

faq.question: Which countries have strong legal protections for the right to food?
faq.answer: India's 2013 National Food Security Act entitles 800 million people to subsidized grain. Brazil's Zero Hunger program dramatically reduced malnutrition. South Africa's constitution explicitly guarantees the right to sufficient food.
